facts.raw_span: a 4-week history of a rapidly growing left caruncular lesion
an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, arising from the caruncle
no evidence of PAM (primary acquired melanosis)
The specimen measured 8 × 6 × 5 mm and had a 4-mm ulceration with necrotic tissue on its surface
Revealed a solid tumor with an inflamed crust on its surface, composed of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity
Showed positive reactivity to melanocytic markers HMB45, MITF2, and Melan-A
The Ki-67 proliferation marker showed a significant number of cycling cells
Sentinel lymph node biopsy findings were negative
Conjunctival and orbital biopsies revealed no tumor
Ulcerated, pedunculated, caruncular tumor
Mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells
Melanoma cells showing immunoreactivity for Melan-A

concepts.why: The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass with anaplastic cells and positive reactivity to melanocytic markers supports this diagnosis.
The absence of pigmentation and the presence of anaplastic cells with mitotic activity support this diagnosis.
The presence of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity and a high proliferative index supports this diagnosis.
The presence of a melanoma in the caruncle, a part of the ocular adnexa, supports this diagnosis.
The absence of systemic disease and the presence of a primary melanoma in the caruncle support this diagnosis.
The presence of a rapidly growing, ulcerated, pedunculated mass in the caruncle supports this diagnosis.

concepts.preferred_label: Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma is not supported, however, Nodular Fasciitis is not relevant here. Consider Undifferentiated Carcinoma of the Caruncle
concepts.why: The ulcerated surface and anaplastic cells with mitotic activity in the specimen are explained by this rare entity.

rationales.F01: Rapid growth of the caruncular lesion suggests a malignant process.
rationales.F02: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface is highly suggestive of a malignant melanoma.
rationales.F05: The presence of large anaplastic cells with mitotic activity is indicative of a high-grade malignancy.
rationales.F06: Positive reactivity to melanocytic markers confirms the diagnosis of melanoma.
rationales.F11: The presence of mitotically active tumor containing anaplastic epithelioid cells is highly suggestive of anaplastic melanoma.
rationales.F12: Immunoreactivity for Melan-A confirms the diagnosis of melanoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of an amelanotic, pedunculated mass with an ulcerated surface, positive reactivity to melanocytic markers, and a high proliferative index supports the diagnosis of Primary Melanoma of the Caruncle, with Anaplastic Melanoma as a close runner-up due to the presence of anaplastic cells with mitotic activity.
